function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + schemas. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs. COMPLETED: Extensive contract + backend inspection. Mapped OpenAPI schemas (RoleWork, RoleWorkItem, SampleWorkItem, SampleState, SampleLifecycle, JourneyPlan, WorkerJourneyPlan, WorkerJourney, JourneyWorkItem, AssignmentWorkItem, LocationFunction, Coordinate, OperationsState, OperationsLocation, OperationsConnection, AuditEntry, AuditSearchResult, ServiceabilityRegion, TimelineEntry, Capacity, Certification, Location, RealtimeEvent, RequesterJourneyPlan, Role, ErrorEnvelope). Reviewed backend handlers: work.go, ws.go, requests.go, users.go, db.go, util.go, journeys.go, assignments.go, main.go, httpx.go. Reviewed schema/mongo.js, schema/postgres.sql, go.mod. Reviewed frontend skeleton (api.ts SAMPLE_TYPES/ROLES, styles.css tokens, package.json) and ui.contract.json scenarios.

PENDING: Lock remaining backend response shapes to OpenAPI; implement/complete frontend to satisfy UI contract scenarios; populate app-setup artifacts; close remaining contract mismatches.

CURRENT_STATE: Agent is mid-exploration, about to lock backend response shapes then build frontend + app-setup. app-setup/ is empty. Frontend has scaffolding only (no main App/components yet).

CODE_STATE:
- backend/: Go 1.22 module lablogistics; Store{PG, Mongo, Audit}; handlers for auth, role work, requests, journeys (handleEditActivePlan), assignments (expireOffers), websocket (lab-logistics-v1)
- schema/postgres.sql: users + locations with fn_collection_point/transfer_point/hub/laboratory
- schema/mongo.js: audit_entries (idempotent drop+recreate)
- frontend/: Vite/React/TS; maplibre-gl + pmtiles; src/api.ts, styles.css only
- contracts/openapi.contract.json + ui.contract.json (scenarios: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshnes…)

DEPS: github.com/google/uuid, gorilla/websocket, lib/pq, mongo-driver, golang.org/x/crypto; frontend react 18.3, maplibre-gl 4.7, pmtiles 3.2

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Working in /workspace; no branch/PR/commit info in events
I'll keep mapping the remaining backend handlers, UI contract, and frontend scaffolding so I can lock response shapes and finish the app.

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open('/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json') as f:
    spec = json.load(f)
schemas = spec['components']['schemas']

print('======== JourneyPlan remaining ========')
print(json.dumps(schemas['JourneyPlan'], indent=2)[2000:])

print('\n======== OperationsState full ========')
print(json.dumps(schemas['OperationsState'], indent=2))

# key remaining endpoints
for path, method in [
    ('/api/authenticate-user','post'),
    ('/api/select-active-role','post'),
    ('/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}','get'),
    ('/api/ui/bootstrap','get'),
    ('/api/accept-assignment','post'),
    ('/api/decline-assignment','post'),
    ('/api/collect-and-seal-sample','post'),
    ('/api/record-worker-location','post'),
    ('/api/update-assignment-progress','post'),
    ('/api/initiate-handoff','post'),
    ('/api/confirm-handoff','post'),
    ('/api/record-handling-checkpoint','post'),
    ('/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt','post'),
    ('/api/record-laboratory-exception','post'),
    ('/api/set-worker-availability','post'),
    ('/api/set-location-status','post'),
    ('/api/set-location-function-status','post'),
    ('/api/set-connection-status','post'),
    ('/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance','post'),
    ('/api/report-disruption','post'),
    ('/api/ingest-presealed-sample','post'),
    ('/ready','get'),
]:
    op = spec['paths'][path][method]
    print(f'\n===== {method.upper()} {path} ({op.get("operationId")}) =====')
    print('security:', op.get('security'))
    rb = op.get('requestBody',{})
    if rb:
        schema = rb.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema',{})
        print('REQ required:', schema.get('required'))
        print('REQ props:', list(schema.get('properties',{}).keys()))
    for code, resp in op.get('responses',{}).items():
        if not code.startswith('2'): continue
        content = resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{})
        if not content:
            print(f'  {code}: no json')
            continue
        sch = content.get('schema',{})
        data = sch.get('properties',{}).get('data')
        if data:
            print(f'  {code} data required:', data.get('required'))
            print(f'  {code} data props:', list(data.get('properties',{}).keys()) if data.get('properties') else data)
            if data.get('$ref'):
                print(f'  {code} $ref:', data['$ref'])
            print(json.dumps(data, indent=2)[:1800])
        else:
            print(f'  {code}:', json.dumps(sch, indent=2)[:1500])
PY"}

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + schemas. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs. Handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Align backend response shapes to OpenAPI contract (IN PROGRESS)
- Build missing frontend UI and app-setup artifacts (PENDING)
- Lock remaining OpenAPI schemas / contract mismatches (IN PROGRESS)

COMPLETED:
- Inspected backend handlers: journeys.go (850 lines), assignments.go (838), network.go (766), requests.go (601), users.go (596), serviceability.go (453), audit.go (316), work.go, auth.go (201), models.go (183), db.go (157), main.go (132), httpx.go (103), idempotency.go (59)
- Inspected frontend: styles.css, api.ts, package.json, vite.config.ts, index.html
- Inspected contracts: openapi.contract.json (create/update-location schemas, JourneyStop, JourneyLeg)
- Inspected schema/postgres.sql, go.mod, map style.json
- Identified contract mismatches in location functions, journey plans, assignment progress, collect-and-seal

PENDING:
- Lock remaining backend response shapes against OpenAPI
- Build missing frontend pages/components
- Build app-setup artifacts
- Align location create/update, journey merge, assignment progress, collect-and-seal responses

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend: Go 1.22 module lablogistics; deps uuid, websocket, lib/pq, mongo-driver, x/crypto
- Frontend: React 18 + Vite + maplibre-gl + pmtiles; proxy /api,/ready to :8080
- Roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab
- Sample types: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse (fixed UUIDs)
- Map: Offline Bangalore Light via pmtiles
- DB: PostgreSQL with DROP+CREATE reset; Mongo for timeline/audit
- Key handlers: handleReadJourneyPlan, handleUpdateProgress, handleAuthenticate, handleListRoleWork, collect_and_seal_sample, location CRUD

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open('/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json') as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

keys = [
 '/api/list-role-work',
 '/api/read-sample-lifecycle',
 '/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}',
 '/api/read-journey-plan',
 '/api/ui/bootstrap',
 '/api/update-assignment-progress',
 '/api/merge-journeys',
 '/api/split-journey',
 '/api/edit-active-plan',
 '/api/read-serviceability-snapshot',
 '/api/configure-capacity',
 '/api/initiate-handoff',
 '/api/confirm-handoff',
 '/api/accept-assignment',
 '/api/decline-assignment',
 '/api/create-user',
 '/api/update-user-access',
 '/api/set-worker-availability',
 '/api/create-connection',
 '/api/create-sample-type',
 '/api/record-handling-checkpoint',
 '/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt',
 '/api/record-laboratory-exception',
 '/api/set-location-status',
 '/api/set-location-function-status',
 '/api/set-connection-status',
 '/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance',
 '/api/search-audit-trail',
 '/api/events',
 '/ready',
]
for p in keys:
    print('='*80)
    print(p)
    op = spec['paths'][p]
    for m, d in op.items():
        print(' METHOD', m, 'op', d.get('operationId'))
        if 'requestBody' in d:
            print(' REQUEST', json.dumps(d['requestBody'], indent=2)[:2200])
        for code in ['200','201']:
            if code in d.get('responses',{}):
                print(' RESP', code, json.dumps(d['responses'][code], indent=2)[:2800])
                print()
        # also print 409/400 codes enums
        for code in ['400','401','403','404','409']:
            if code in d.get('responses',{}):
                schema = d['responses'][code]
                try:
                    codes = schema['content']['application/json']['schema']['properties']['code']
                    print(' ERR', code, codes)
                except Exception:
                    pass
PY"}

CODE_STATE:
- Backend: /workspace/backend/{main.go,users.go,httpx.go,db.go,auth.go,requests.go,journeys.go,work.go,models.go,audit.go,assignments.go,ws.go,util.go}

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + schemas. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs. Handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

COMPLETED:
- Explored OpenAPI schemas: RoleWork, SampleWorkItem, JourneyWorkItem, AssignmentWorkItem, SampleLifecycle, SampleState, User, OperationsState, OperationsSample, OperationsWorker, OperationsException, OperationsJourney, JourneyPlan, RequesterJourneyPlan, WorkerJourneyPlan, RoleWorkItem, TimelineEntry, OperationsLocation, OperationsConnection, AuditEntry, AuditSearchResult, Capacity
- Inspected UI contract scenarios (login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshness…)
- Read backend handlers: requests.go, assignments.go, users.go, journeys.go, work.go, audit.go, auth.go, main.go, httpx.go, models.go, db.go, ws.go, util.go
- Read frontend scaffold: api.ts (SAMPLE_TYPES, ROLES), styles.css, vite.config.ts (proxy /api,/ready → :8080), package.json (maplibre-gl, pmtiles, react), index.html, tsconfig.json
- Inspected schema/mongo.js (audit_entries collections) and /opt/arena/map-assets (bangalore.pmtiles)

PENDING:
- Lock backend response shapes to OpenAPI schemas (contract mismatches identified)
- Align remaining handlers with required response contracts
- Build frontend UI to match ui.contract.json scenarios
- Wire map (bangalore.pmtiles + maplibre) and realtime WS (lab-logistics-v1)

CURRENT_STATE:
- Agent in inspection/alignment phase; no systematic code edits applied yet
- Backend: Go Store{PG, Mongo, Audit}; roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab; WS upgrader subprotocol lab-logistics-v1
- Key handlers seen: handleListRoleWork, handleUpdateUserAccess, handleMergeJourneys, expireOffers, create_collection_request / ingest_presealed_sample, writeTimeline
- Frontend: Vite+React+TS, SAMPLE_TYPES Amber/Indigo/Frost/Pulse, design tokens in styles.css
- Map assets: /opt/arena/map-assets/bangalore.pmtiles

CODE_STATE:
- backend/: main.go, models.go, auth.go, db.go, httpx.go, requests.go, assignments.go, journeys.go, work.go, users.go, audit.go, ws.go, util.go
- frontend/src/: api.ts, styles.css, main.tsx (entry)
- contracts/: openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json
- schema/mongo.js

DEPS: Go (lib/pq, mongo-driver, gorilla/websocket, google/uuid, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt); frontend (react 18, maplibre-gl, pmtiles, vite)

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Working tree under /workspace; no branch/PR/commit info observed in these events
I'll continue mapping the existing backend, frontend, and UI contract so I can lock response shapes and build the remaining UI.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

- Go: google/uuid, gorilla/websocket, lib/pq, mongo-driver, golang.org/x/crypto
- Frontend: React/Vite (tsconfig ES2020, bundler resolution)

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

  working directory changes persist across commands.

  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.

  The runtime may not support them reliably.

* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- lock-openapi-shapes: inspect/align backend response shapes to pinned OpenAPI (IN PROGRESS)
- build-frontend: React/Vite UI matching ui.contract.json scenarios (PENDING)
- app-setup: populate /workspace/app-setup (PENDING)

COMPLETED:
- Explored backend, schema, contracts, frontend scaffold, and domain instructions
- Identified contract mismatches; plan is lock OpenAPI response shapes, then frontend + app-setup

PENDING:
- Align backend JSON/response shapes to pinned OpenAPI
- Build remaining frontend (main.tsx, App, role views, maps, sample/timeline UI)
- Implement app-setup
- Verify UI contract scenarios (login, role switch, work views, sample history/freshness, etc.)

CURRENT_STATE: Agent still in inspect-then-fix phase; no confirmed contract-alignment or frontend feature edits yet. Frontend is scaffold-only. app-setup/ is empty.

CODE_STATE:
- Backend (/workspace/backend): main.go, auth.go, users.go, network.go, serviceability.go, journeys.go, assignments.go, work.go, audit.go, idempotency.go, requests.go, models.go, httpx.go, db.go, util.go
- Schema: /workspace/schema/postgres.sql (journeys, users, locations, capacity_pools, etc.)
- Contracts: /workspace/contracts/ui.contract.json (scenarios: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshnes…)
- Frontend scaffold: package.json (lab-logistics-ui, react 18, maplibre-gl, pmtiles, vite), vite.config.ts (proxy /api + /ready → :8080, outDir dist), index.html, src/styles.css, src/api.ts, src/vite-env.d.ts
- Docs: INSTRUCTION.md (domain rules), README.md (frozen public contracts)

DEPS: Go + Postgres/Mongo backend; frontend react/react-dom/maplibre-gl/pmtiles + vite/tsc. No dep changes observed.

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Not observed in these events.
I'll inspect the pinned contracts and remaining frontend/backend gaps before aligning response shapes and building the UI.

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

COMPLETED: Inspected backend modules (assignments.go, journeys.go, requests.go, users.go, go.mod), frontend scaffolding (api.ts, vite-env.d.ts, tsconfig.json), contracts (openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json), map-assets, schema/mongo.js, and workspace structure.

PENDING: Lock backend response shapes to match OpenAPI schemas (SampleState, JourneyPlan, RoleWork, OperationsState, etc.); build React/Vite frontend UI covering all UI contract scenarios; implement app-setup.

CURRENT_STATE: Backend Go module lablogistics (Go 1.22) with handlers for assignments, journeys, requests, auth, users, audit. Frontend is scaffold-only (api.ts with SAMPLE_TYPES/ROLES, no App/components). app-setup/ is empty. Map assets available at /opt/arena/map-assets (Bangalore PMTiles). DATABASE_URL=postgresql://arena:arena@127.0.0.1:5432/arena.

CODE_STATE: Backend files present: assignments.go (handleAcceptAssignment, handleConfirmHandoff), journeys.go (handleReadJourneyPlan, replanJourney), requests.go (createRequestBody), users.go (handleRecordWorkerLocation), auth.go, db.go, httpx.go, idempotency.go, main.go, mongo. function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# dump remaining ops
for p in ["/api/create-sample-type","/api/update-sample-type","/api/update-location","/api/set-location-status","/api/set-location-function-status","/api/create-connection","/api/set-connection-status","/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance","/api/update-user-access"]:
    methods = spec["paths"].get(p, {})
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        print("\n"+"="*70)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  op={op.get('operationId')}")
        if "requestBody" in op:
            for ct, c in op["requestBody"].get("content", {}).items():
                print(" REQUEST:", json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2)[:1600])
        for code, resp in op.get("responses", {}).items():
            if code.startswith("2"):
                for ct, c in resp.get("content", {}).items():
                    print(f" RESP {code}:", json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2)[:1600])

# OperationsState remaining required
print("\n\nOperationsState required:")
print(spec["components"]["schemas"]["OperationsState"].get("required"))
print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["OperationsState"]["properties"], indent=2)[-800:])

# create-collection-request required
print("\ncreate request data required:")
schema = spec["paths"]["/api/create-collection-request"]["post"]["responses"]["201"]["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]["properties"]["data"]
print(schema.get("required"))

print("\nconfirm lab receipt request:")
print(json.dumps(spec["paths"]["/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt"]["post"]["requestBody"], indent=2)[:1200])
PY","summary":"Dump remaining admin API contracts"}

Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

security_risk.description:
Security risk levels for actions.

Based on OpenHands security risk levels but adapted for agent-sdk.
Integer values allow for easy comparison and ordering.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `undo_edit`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory.

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace.

new_str.description: Optional parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if not given, no string will be added). Required parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert.

insert_line.description: Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If none is given, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

function.name: think
function.description:
Use the tool to think about something. It will not obtain new information or make any changes to the repository, but just log the thought. Use it when complex reasoning or brainstorming is needed.

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.
2. After receiving test results, use this tool to brainstorm ways to fix failing tests.
3. When planning a complex refactoring, use this tool to outline different approaches and their tradeoffs.
4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.

* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

for p in [
    "/api/ui/bootstrap","/api/list-role-work","/api/read-sample-lifecycle",
    "/api/read-journey-plan","/api/set-location-status","/api/set-location-function-status",
    "/api/create-connection","/api/set-connection-status","/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance",
    "/api/update-user-access"
]:

    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        print("\n"+"="*70)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  op={op.get('operationId')}")
        if "requestBody" in op:
            for ct, c in op["requestBody"].get("content", {}).items():
                print(" REQUEST:", json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2)[:2500])
        for code, resp in op.get("responses", {}).items():
            if str(code).startswith("2"):
                for ct, c in resp.get("content", {}).items():

# JourneyPlan remaining properties
print("\n==== JourneyPlan full")
print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["JourneyPlan"], indent=2)[:5000])

print("\n==== ui bootstrap request params")
print(json.dumps(spec["paths"]["/api/ui/bootstrap"], indent=2)[:4000])
PY"}

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

message.content: I need a complete picture of remaining contract mismatches before locking response shapes and building the UI. I'll dump the rest of the OpenAPI responses and inspect the remaining backend files.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# dump remaining operation responses
for path, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        print(f"\n######## {oid} {m.upper()} {path}")
        if "requestBody" in op:
            rb = op["requestBody"]
            schema = rb.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{}).get("schema",{})
            print(" REQUEST required:", schema.get("required"))
            print(" REQUEST props:", list(schema.get("properties",{}).keys()))
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            content = resp.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{}).get("schema",{})
            if "properties" in content:
                props = content.get("properties",{})
                if "data" in props:
                    data = props["data"]
                    print(f"  {code} data required:", data.get("required"))
                    print(f"  {code} data props:", list(data.get("properties",{}).keys())[:40])
                    if "$ref" in data:
                        print(f"  {code} data $ref:", data["$ref"])
                    if "allOf" in data:
                        print(f"  {code} data allOf:", data["allOf"])
                else:
                    print(f"  {code} props:", list(props.keys()))
            elif "$ref" in content:
                print(f"  {code} $ref:", content["$ref"])
            else:
                print(f"  {code}:", json.dumps(content)[:300])

print("\n==== JourneyPlan full required + props ====")
jp = spec["components"]["schemas"]["JourneyPlan"]
print("required:", jp.get("required"))
print("props:", list(jp.get("properties",{}).keys()))

print("\n==== OperationsState full ====")
os_ = spec["components"]["schemas"]["OperationsState"]
print("required:", os_.get("required"))
print("props:", list(os_.get("properties",{}).keys()))
print(json.dumps(os_, indent=2)[:8000])
PY","summary":"Dump all OpenAPI operation request/response shapes"}

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Inspect remaining backend handlers, UI contract, and app-setup to lock API response shapes (IN PROGRESS)
- Fix journey-plan payload: uses `stops`/`assignments` instead of contract's `orderedStops`/`legs` (PENDING)
- Build/complete frontend to match UI contract scenarios (PENDING)

COMPLETED: Inspected backend files (assignments.go, journeys.go, requests.go, network.go, audit.go, work.go, httpx.go, main.go, models.go, auth.go, users.go), frontend scaffolding (index.html, vite.config.ts, styles.css, tsconfig.json, api.ts, package.json), schema (mongo.js, postgres.sql), contracts (openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json), README.md, INSTRUCTION.md. Extracted OpenAPI paths and key schemas (JourneyStop, JourneyLeg, SampleLifecycle, SampleWorkItem, JourneyWorkItem, AssignmentWorkItem, Capacity, OperationsConnection, RealtimeEvent, AuditSearchResult, ServiceabilityRegion, ErrorEnvelope). UI contract scenarios include: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshnes...

PENDING:
- Lock remaining API response shapes to OpenAPI contract
- Fix journey-plan payload field names (`orderedStops`/`legs`)
- Complete frontend UI to match all contract scenarios
- Verify remaining backend handlers (assignments, journeys, requests, network, audit, work)

CURRENT_STATE: Agent is inspecting leftover backend handlers, UI assets, and setup scripts to lock API shapes before finishing the frontend. Journey-plan still mismatches contract field names.

CODE_STATE:
- backend/: assignments.go (handoff confirm logic ~L580), journeys.go (handleReadJourneyPlan), requests.go (createRequestBody), network.go (funcsFromList), audit.go (writeTimeline), work.go (handleListRoleWork), httpx.go (apiError/errJSON), main.go (openStore/ensureAdmin), models.go (role constants), auth.go (Session), users.go (handleAuthenticate)
- frontend/: Vite+React+TS, maplibre-gl + pmtiles, SAMPLE_TYPES and ROLES in api.ts, styles with lab-logistics palette
- contracts/: openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json (version 1, product lab-sample-pickup-and-delivery)
- schema/: postgres.sql (idempotent DROP+CREATE), mongo.js (audit_entries etc.)

DEPS: Go backend (google/uuid, mongo-driver, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt); frontend (react 18.3, maplibre-gl 4.7, pmtiles 3.2, Vite)

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Working in /workspace; no branch/commit info observed

I have a clearer picture of the remaining contract mismatches. Next I’ll inspect the journey-plan builder, remaining handlers, and the UI contract so I can lock the API shapes before finishing the frontend.

  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)
print("openapi", spec.get("openapi"))
print("info", spec.get("info",{}).get("title"), spec.get("info",{}).get("version"))
print("\n=== PATHS ===")
for path, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for method, op in methods.items():
        if method.startswith("x-"): continue
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        codes = list(op.get("responses",{}).keys())
        print(f"{method.upper():6} {path:50} {oid:40} {codes}")
print("\n=== COMPONENTS SCHEMAS ===")
for name in spec.get("components",{}).get("schemas",{}):
    print(" ", name)
print("\n=== SECURITY ===")
print(spec.get("security"))
print(spec.get("components",{}).get("securitySchemes"))
PY"}

* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep

* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# auth, select role, create user, update user, read user, ingest, cancel, reroute, edit, update progress, set worker avail, events
ops = [
    "/api/authenticate-user",
    "/api/select-active-role",
    "/api/create-user",
    "/api/update-user-access",
    "/api/read-user/{userId}",
    "/api/ingest-presealed-sample",
    "/api/cancel-journey",
    "/api/reroute-journey",
    "/api/edit-active-plan",
    "/api/update-assignment-progress",
    "/api/set-worker-availability",
    "/api/events",
    "/api/read-journey-plan",
    "/api/split-journey",
    "/api/merge-journeys",
    "/api/record-handling-checkpoint",
    "/api/record-laboratory-exception",
]
for p in ops:
    methods = spec["paths"][p]
    for m, op in methods.items():
        print("="*80)
        print(m.upper(), p, op.get("operationId"))
        # security
        print("security:", op.get("security", spec.get("security")))
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            print("REQUEST:")
            print(json.dumps(rb, indent=2)[:2500])
        for code in ["200","201"]:
            if code in op.get("responses", {}):
                print(f"--- {code} ---")
                print(json.dumps(op["responses"][code], indent=2)[:2500])
        print()

print("SECURITY SCHEMES:")

print("GLOBAL SECURITY:", spec.get("security"))
print("INFO:", json.dumps(spec.get("info"), indent=2)[:500])
print("SERVERS:", spec.get("servers"))
print("OPENAPI:", spec.get("openapi"))

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

When exploring project structure, start with this directory instead of the root filesystem.

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

for name in ["WorkerJourneyPlan","RequesterJourneyPlan"]:
    print("="*80)
    print(name)
    print(json.dumps(schemas[name], indent=2))

# remaining response schemas for key ops
ops = [
    "/api/check-serviceability",
    "/api/create-collection-request",
    "/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}",
    "/api/read-sample-lifecycle",
    "/api/list-role-work",
    "/api/accept-assignment",
    "/api/decline-assignment",
    "/api/collect-and-seal-sample",
    "/api/record-worker-location",
    "/api/initiate-handoff",
    "/api/confirm-handoff",
    "/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt",
    "/api/read-operations-state",
    "/api/read-serviceability-snapshot",
    "/api/search-audit-trail",
    "/api/ui/bootstrap",
    "/api/create-location",
    "/api/update-location",
    "/api/set-location-status",
    "/api/set-location-function-status",
    "/api/create-connection",
    "/api/set-connection-status",
    "/api/configure-capacity",
    "/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance",
    "/api/create-sample-type",
    "/api/update-sample-type",
    "/api/cancel-journey",
    "/api/reroute-journey",
    "/api/report-disruption",
    "/ready",
]
for p in ops:
    methods = spec["paths"][p]
    for m, op in methods.items():
        print("="*80)
        print(m.upper(), p, op.get("operationId"))
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            schema = rb["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]
            print("REQUEST required:", schema.get("required"))
            print("REQUEST props:", list(schema.get("properties",{}).keys()))
        for code, resp in op.get("responses", {}).items():
            if code.startswith("2"):
                print(f"--- {code} ---")
                content = resp.get("content", {})
                for ct, body in content.items():
                    s = body.get("schema", {})
                    print(json.dumps(s, indent=2)[:3000])
        print()
