USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

COMPLETED: Extensive backend/contract inspection (no code edits yet). Mapped handlers, schema, OpenAPI ops, and frontend scaffolding.

PENDING:
- Fix backend response-shape / route mismatches vs pinned OpenAPI
- Build real React/Vite UI (currently scaffolding)
- Fill empty app-setup
- Align remaining handlers (auth, users, ingest, cancel, reroute, edit plan, progress, worker availability, events)

CURRENT_STATE: Agent is in inspect-then-fix phase. Backend largely present but diverges from contract; frontend is scaffolding + styles only.

CODE_STATE:
- Backend (Go): main.go routes (auth, users, requests, journeys, assignments, network, serviceability, work, audit, bootstrap, events/WS); files: httpx.go, models.go, auth.go, audit.go, journeys.go, assignments.go (handoff both-side confirm + seal/temp/container checks), users.go, requests.go, db.go (Store: PG+Mongo), network.go, serviceability.go, ws.go (lab-logistics-v1), util.go, work.go
- Schema: /workspace/schema/postgres.sql (journeys: journey_id, parent_journey_id, plan_version, route_mode, status, estimated_delivery_at, total_cost_units…)
- Frontend: Vite/TS React; tsconfig ES2020 bundler; styles.css design tokens only
- Contract: /workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json (ops include authenticate-user, select-active-role, create/update/read-user, ingest, cancel, reroute, edit, update-progress, set-worker-avail, events)
- Roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab…

DEPS: Go: lib/pq, mongo-driver, gorilla/websocket, google/uuid, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt. Frontend: React/Vite TS.

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Unknown; working in /workspace.
I'll keep mapping the remaining contract mismatches, then fix backend responses, build the UI, and fill app-setup.

import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:

print("info", spec.get("info",{}).get("title"), spec.get("info",{}).get("version"))

for p, methods in spec["paths"].items():

# login

auth = spec["paths"]["/api/authenticate-user"]["post"]
print("operationId", auth.get("operationId"))
print(json.dumps(auth.get("responses",{}).get("200"), indent=2)[:2000])

print("\n=== BOOTSTRAP ===")
if "/api/read-ui-bootstrap" in spec["paths"]:
    print(json.dumps(spec["paths"]["/api/read-ui-bootstrap"], indent=2)[:3000])
else:
    print("no bootstrap path")

print("\n=== LIST ROLE WORK ===")
print(json.dumps(spec["paths"]["/api/list-role-work"], indent=2)[:4000])
PY","summary":"Extract OpenAPI paths and key schemas"}

function.description:

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

import json

for p, methods in paths.items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        print("="*80)
        print(m.upper(), p, op.get("operationId"))
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            schema = rb["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]
            print("REQ required:", schema.get("required"))
            print("REQ props:", {k: (v.get('type') or v.get('$ref') or v.get('enum')) for k,v in schema.get("properties",{}).items()})
        print("RESP codes:", list(op.get("responses",{}).keys()))
        for code in ("200","201"):
            if code not in op.get("responses",{}):
                continue
            content = op["responses"][code].get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                s = body.get("schema",{})
                data = s.get("properties",{}).get("data", s)
                print(f"--- {code} data required:", data.get("required"))
                print(f"--- {code} data props:", list(data.get("properties",{}).keys()) if data.get("properties") else data)
        # error codes
        err_codes = {}
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if code in ("200","201"): continue
            content = resp.get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                s = body.get("schema",{})
                props = s.get("properties",{})
                c = props.get("code",{})
                err_codes[code] = c.get("enum")
        print("ERR:", err_codes)
        print()

print("\n=== Coordinate ===")

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

schemas = spec["components"]["schemas"]
print("ALL SCHEMAS:", list(schemas.keys()))
print()
for name in ["RoleWork","RoleWorkItem","OperationsState","OperationsSample","OperationsWorker","OperationsRoute","OperationsHandoff","OperationsDelay","OperationsException","AssignmentCountSpread","AuditSearchResult","AuditEntry","TimelineEntry","TimelineEvent","JourneyPlan","JourneyStop","JourneyAssignment","SampleState","SampleLifecycle","ServiceabilitySnapshot","ServiceabilityCheck","User","UserAccess","Bootstrap","Handoff","HandlingCheckpoint","Assignment"]:
    if name in schemas:
        s = schemas[name]
        print("="*60)
        print(name)
        print("required:", s.get("required"))
        print("props:", list(s.get("properties",{}).keys()))
        print(json.dumps(s, indent=2)[:2500])
        print()

print("\n\n=== PATHS ===")
for p in spec["paths"]:
    print(p, list(spec["paths"][p].keys()))

print("\n\n=== remaining ops I missed ===")
for p, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        if oid in ("authenticate_user","accept_assignment","check_serviceability","create_collection_request","configure_capacity","configure_laboratory_acceptance","confirm_handoff","confirm_laboratory_receipt","collect_and_seal_sample","cancel_journey","create_connection","set_location_status","set_worker_availability","split_journey","read_ui_bootstrap","update_assignment_progress","update_location","update_sample_type","update_user_access","system_readiness"):
            continue
        print(m.upper(), p, oid)
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            schema = rb["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]
            print("  REQ required:", schema.get("required"))
            print("  REQ props:", list(schema.get("properties",{}).keys()))
        for code in ("200","201"):
            if code not in op.get("responses",{}):
                continue
            content = op["responses"][code].get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                s = body.get("schema",{})

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

COMPLETED: Inventoried OpenAPI schemas and existing backend/schema/frontend scaffolding. Extracted remaining contract schemas (RoleWork, Operations*, Sample/Journey/AssignmentWorkItem, JourneyLeg, LocationFunctionStates, Worker/RequesterJourneyPlan). Read backend modules and DB schemas to identify contract mismatches.

PENDING: Fix backend response shapes to match OpenAPI; then build frontend and app-setup.

CURRENT_STATE: Exploration/inventory phase complete. Agent intends to lock response shapes next, then frontend. Map tiles present (bangalore.pmtiles, fonts, sprites). Frontend is Vite/TS React (tsconfig exists). No code edits applied yet in this window.

CODE_STATE:
- backend/: main.go, auth.go, users.go, db.go, models.go, httpx.go, util.go, idempotency.go, requests.go, assignments.go, journeys.go, network.go, serviceability.go, work.go, audit.go
- Store: PG *sql.DB + Mongo client/audit collection
- Roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab
- schema/postgres.sql: idempotent DROP+CREATE
- schema/mongo.js: audit_entries (+ others), db arena
- contracts/openapi.contract.json: source of truth for response shapes
- frontend/tsconfig.json: ES2020, bundler resolution, noEmit

DEPS: github.com/lib/pq, mongo-driver, google/uuid, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Working in /workspace; branch/commit not observed in this window
I'll inspect the remaining backend, UI contract, and frontend scaffolding so I can lock response shapes and then implement the app.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

Based on OpenHands security risk levels but adapted for agent-sdk.
Integer values allow for easy comparison and ordering.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# Dump request bodies and 2xx responses for all operations
for p, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        print("="*80)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  op={op.get('operationId')}")
        # params
        params = op.get("parameters") or []
        if params:
            print(" PARAMS:", json.dumps(params)[:800])
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content = rb.get("content", {}).get("application/json", {})
            schema = content.get("schema")
            print(" REQUEST:", json.dumps(schema, indent=2)[:2200])
        resps = op.get("responses", {})
        for code in sorted(resps):
            if code.startswith("2") or code in ("200","201","204"):
                r = resps[code]
                c = (r.get("content") or {}).get("application/json", {})
                print(f" RESP {code}:", json.dumps(c.get("schema"), indent=2)[:2500])
        # also print 4xx codes
        codes = list(resps.keys())
        print(" ALL STATUS:", codes)

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

wanted = [
    "/api/decline-assignment",
    "/api/edit-active-plan",
    "/api/events",
    "/api/ingest-presealed-sample",
    "/api/initiate-handoff",
    "/api/list-role-work",
    "/api/merge-journeys",
    "/api/read-journey-plan",
    "/api/read-operations-state",
    "/api/read-sample-lifecycle",
]
for p in wanted:
    methods = spec["paths"][p]
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        print("="*80)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  op={op.get('operationId')}")
        params = op.get("parameters")
        if params:
            print(" PARAMS:", json.dumps(params)[:600])
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content = rb.get("content", {}).get("application/json", {})
            schema = content.get("schema")
            print(" REQUEST:", json.dumps(schema, indent=2)[:2200])
        resps = op.get("responses", {})
        for code in sorted(resps):
            if str(code).startswith("2"):
                r = resps[code]
                c = (r.get("content") or {}).get("application/json", {})
                print(f" RESP {code}:", json.dumps(c.get("schema"), indent=2)[:3500])
        print(" ALL STATUS:", list(resps.keys()))
        for code in ["400","403","409"]:
            if code in resps:
                r = resps[code]
                c = (r.get("content") or {}).get("application/json", {})
                sch = c.get("schema")
                if sch:
                    props = (sch.get("properties") or {})
                    if "code" in props:

print(json.dumps(spec.get("security"), indent=2))

print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["RealtimeEvent"], indent=2))
print("\n==== ServiceabilityRegion ====")
print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["ServiceabilityRegion"], indent=2))
print("\n==== Capacity ====")
print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["Capacity"], indent=2))
print("\n==== Certification ====")
print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["Certification"], indent=2))
print("\n==== Role ====")
print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"]["Role"], indent=2))
print("\n==== Coordinate ====")

print("\n==== LocationFunction ====")

            print("...TRUNC...", s[3500:7000])

  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,

  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# dump 200/201 data schema details for key ops
for p, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        for code in ["200","201"]:
            resp = op.get("responses", {}).get(code)
            if not resp: continue
            content = resp.get("content", {}).get("application/json", {})
            sch = content.get("schema", {})
            props = sch.get("properties", {})
            data = props.get("data", {})
            print(f"\n## {op.get('operationId')} {code} data:")
            if "$ref" in data:
                print("  $ref", data["$ref"])
            elif "properties" in data:
                print("  keys:", list(data["properties"].keys()))
                print("  required:", data.get("required"))
                print("  addl:", data.get("additionalProperties"))
                for k,v in data["properties"].items():
                    extra = ""
                    if "$ref" in v: extra = v["$ref"]
                    elif "enum" in v: extra = f"enum={v['enum']}"
                    elif v.get("type")=="array":
                        extra = f"array of {v.get('items',{})}"
                    elif "properties" in v:
                        extra = f"obj keys={list(v['properties'].keys())} req={v.get('required')}"
                    print(f"    {k}: {v.get('type','')} {extra}")
            elif "oneOf" in data:
                print("  oneOf:")
                for item in data["oneOf"]:
                    print("   ", item)
            else:
                print(" ", json.dumps(data)[:800])

print("\n\n==== security schemes ====")
print(json.dumps(spec.get("components",{}).get("securitySchemes",{}), indent=2))
print("info:", json.dumps(spec.get("info",{}), indent=2)[:500])
print("servers:", spec.get("servers"))
print("openapi:", spec.get("openapi"))
PY","summary":"Dump response data schemas for all ops"}

- Session: Token, UserID, Username, FullName, ActiveRole, Roles

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

message.content: I have a clearer picture of the remaining contract mismatches. Next I'll dump the remaining OpenAPI operation shapes and the rest of the backend so I can lock responses and finish the frontend.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# Dump remaining schemas that were clipped
for name in ["WorkerJourneyPlan", "RequesterJourneyPlan", "OperationsState"]:
    print("="*80)
    print(name)
    print(json.dumps(spec["components"]["schemas"][name], indent=2))
    print()

# Dump request/response for key operations
ops_of_interest = [
    "authenticate_user", "select_active_role", "list_role_work",
    "read_operations_state", "read_journey_plan", "read_sample_lifecycle",
    "read_sample_state", "edit_active_plan", "ingest_presealed_sample",
    "initiate_handoff", "check_serviceability", "create_collection_request",
    "read_ui_bootstrap", "search_audit_trail", "accept_assignment",
    "decline_assignment", "collect_and_seal_sample", "record_worker_location",
    "create_user", "create_location", "read_serviceability_snapshot",
    "stream_realtime_events", "system_readiness", "confirm_handoff",
    "split_journey", "merge_journeys", "cancel_journey", "reroute_journey",
    "report_disruption", "configure_capacity", "update_assignment_progress",
]
print("\n\n===== OPERATIONS =====\n")
for p, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        if oid not in ops_of_interest:
            continue
        print("="*80)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  [{oid}]")
        print("security:", op.get("security"))
        if "parameters" in op:
            print("params:", json.dumps(op["parameters"], indent=2)[:1500])
        if "requestBody" in op:
            rb = op["requestBody"]
            print("requestBody required:", rb.get("required"))
            content = rb.get("content", {})
            for ct, c in content.items():
                print(f"  {ct}:", json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2)[:3000])
        print("responses:")
        for code, resp in op.get("responses", {}).items():
            print(f"  {code}: {resp.get('description')}")
            content = resp.get("content", {})
            for ct, c in content.items():
                s = json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2)
                print(f"    {ct}: {s[:2500]}")
        print()
PY","summary":"Dump remaining OpenAPI schemas and operations"}

        print()

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- inventory-backend: IN_PROGRESS — remaining handlers, API shapes, contract mismatches
- lock-api-shapes: PENDING — dump remaining OpenAPI ops and align backend responses
- seed-default-data: PENDING
- build-frontend: PENDING — React/Vite UI matching ui.contract.json scenarios
- app-setup: PENDING — empty app-setup/ dir still needs scripts

COMPLETED:
- Inventoried most backend files: work.go, auth.go, users.go, httpx.go, models.go, db.go, assignments.go, journeys.go, audit.go, requests.go, network.go, serviceability.go, ws.go, main.go
- Inventoried schemas: postgres.sql, mongo.js
- Inventoried contracts: openapi.contract.json (paths + most schemas), ui.contract.json (scenarios)
- Inventoried frontend skeleton: api.ts, styles.css, package.json, vite.config.ts, index.html; missing main.tsx/App
- Inventoried INSTRUCTION.md domain rules

PENDING:
- Finish remaining backend handler/contract alignment (assignments, journeys edit, users update, request create response)
- Extract remaining OpenAPI operation request/response shapes
- Seed default/admin data
- Build full React frontend (main.tsx + views for all UI scenarios)
- Write app-setup scripts
- Verify contract match end-to-end

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend largely implemented in /workspace/backend/*.go with Store over PG+Mongo
- Roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab
- Frontend src only has api.ts + styles.css; no React app entry yet
- app-setup/ and bin/ exist but empty
- OpenAPI schemas extracted for most components; WorkerJourneyPlan, RequesterJourneyPlan, OperationsState dumped; remaining ops still being extracted
- UI scenarios include: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshness_visible_to_owner, sample_view_shows_location_custodian...

CODE_STATE:
- backend/main.go: openStore(), ensureAdmin(), HTTP routes + WS
- backend/auth.go: Session{Token,UserID,Username,FullName,ActiveRole,Roles}
- backend/models.go: Role* constants, domain types
- backend/db.go: Store{PG,Mongo,Audit}
- backend/requests.go: createRequestBody, handleCreate returns requestId/sampleId/serviceability
- backend/ws.go: gorilla websocket, subprotocol lab-logistics-v1
- frontend/src/api.ts: SAMPLE_TYPES, ROLES constants
- frontend/vite.config.ts: proxy /api,/ready to :8080; build outDir dist

DEPS: Go: lib/pq, mongo-driver, gorilla/websocket, google/uuid, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt. Frontend: react 18, maplibre-gl, pmtiles, vite.

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Workspace at /workspace; no branch/PR activity noted.
I'll inventory the remaining backend handlers, UI contract, and app-setup gaps so I can finish the contract-aligned stack.

  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

- Read OpenAPI response schemas: RoleWork, RoleWorkItem, SampleState, SampleLifecycle, JourneyPlan, RequesterJourneyPlan, WorkerJourneyPlan, OperationsState, AuditSearchResult, AuditEntry, Location, LocationFunctionStates, LocationFunction, Certification, RealtimeEvent, Serviceability

- Reviewed map style: Offline Bangalore Light (pmtiles)

PENDING:
- Finish backend OpenAPI contract alignment (response shapes for list_role_work, read_operations_state, read_journey_plan, read_sample_lifecycle, read_sample_state, edit_active_plan, ingest_presealed_sample, initiate_handoff, check_serviceability, create_collection_request, create_user, etc.)
- Build frontend matching UI contract scenarios
- App-setup wiring/scripts

- Backend exists with substantial handlers (auth, assignments, journeys, network, requests, work, audit, websocket) but response shapes still being locked to OpenAPI
- Frontend is a Vite/React skeleton with api.ts constants, styles, and proxy config — not yet built out

- DEPS: github.com/google/uuid, github.com/gorilla/websocket, github.com/lib/pq, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt

- Store: PG (*sql.DB) + Mongo (audit_entries collection)
- Session: Token, UserID, Username, FullName, ActiveRole, Roles
- Vite proxy: /api and /ready → 127.0.0.1:8080

DEPS: Go 1.22 + Postgres + Mongo; React 18 + Vite + MapLibre + PMTiles

   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.

message.content: I need to lock remaining API shapes to the contract, then finish the frontend and app-setup. I'll start by extracting every request/response schema and comparing it with the current handlers.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# dump request bodies and success responses for all operations
for p, methods in spec["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        print("="*80)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  [{oid}]")
        print("summary:", op.get("summary","")[:200])
        print("security:", op.get("security"))
        if "parameters" in op:
            print("params:", json.dumps(op["parameters"], indent=2)[:1500])
        if "requestBody" in op:
            rb = op["requestBody"]
            print("requestBody required:", rb.get("required"))
            content = rb.get("content", {})
            for ct, c in content.items():
                print("content:", ct)
                print(json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2)[:5000])
        print("responses:")
        for code, resp in op.get("responses", {}).items():
            print(f"  {code}: {resp.get('description','')[:120]}")
            content = resp.get("content", {})
            for ct, c in content.items():
                print(f"    {ct}:")
                print("    " + json.dumps(c.get("schema", {}), indent=2).replace("\n", "\n    ")[:4000])
        print()
PY","summary":"Dump all OpenAPI request/response contracts"}

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

        for code, resp in op.get("responses", {}).items():
            if str(code).startswith("2"):

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.

  working directory changes persist across commands.

  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

message.content:
USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

COMPLETED: Surveyed backend handlers, models, contracts, and frontend scaffold to lock API/UI shapes before implementing missing pieces.

PENDING: Lock leftover API response shapes to OpenAPI schemas; implement remaining backend contract mismatches; build frontend (main/App/map/role views); implement app-setup scripts; match all UI contract scenarios.

CURRENT_STATE: Agent mid-survey, about to lock response shapes then build frontend/map/app-setup. Backend largely implemented; frontend is Vite/React scaffold only (no App/main yet); app-setup empty.

CODE_STATE:
- Backend (/workspace/backend): main.go, models.go, httpx.go, work.go, users.go, assignments.go, journeys.go, auth.go, requests.go, network.go, db.go, audit.go, idempotency.go. Store uses Postgres + Mongo. Roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab. Sample lifecycle includes sealing, journeys, dual-confirm handoffs, timeline, audit.
- Frontend (/workspace/frontend): package.json (react 18, vite, maplibre-gl, pmtiles), vite.config.ts (proxy /api,/ready → :8080), index.html, src/api.ts (SAMPLE_TYPES Amber/Indigo/Frost/Pulse + ROLES), src/styles.css. Missing main.tsx/App and feature views.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep

* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

for name in ["SampleState","SampleLifecycle","SampleWorkItem","JourneyWorkItem","AssignmentWorkItem","RoleWork","RoleWorkItem","OperationsState","AuditSearchResult","AuditEntry","JourneyStop","JourneyLeg","JourneyPlan","RealtimeEvent","ErrorEnvelope"]:
    s = spec["components"]["schemas"].get(name)
    print("="*70, name)
    print(json.dumps(s, indent=2) if s else "MISSING")

print("\n\n======= AUTH + SELECT ROLE + CREATE USER + READ USER + BOOTSTRAP + EVENTS + OPS + LIFECYCLE + JOURNEY + SERVICEABILITY SNAPSHOT =======")
wanted = [
    "/api/authenticate-user",
    "/api/select-active-role",
    "/api/create-user",
    "/api/update-user-access",
    "/api/read-user/{userId}",
    "/api/ui/bootstrap",
    "/api/events",
    "/api/read-operations-state",
    "/api/read-serviceability-snapshot",
    "/api/create-collection-request",
    "/api/ingest-presealed-sample",
    "/api/create-location",
    "/api/update-location",
    "/api/set-location-status",
    "/api/set-location-function-status",
    "/ready",
]
for p in wanted:
    methods = spec["paths"].get(p, {})
    for m, op in methods.items():
        print("="*70)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  op={op.get('operationId')}  codes={list(op.get('responses',{}).keys())}")
        print("security", op.get("security", "default"))
        if "parameters" in op:
            print("PARAMS", json.dumps(op["parameters"], indent=2)[:1500])
        if "requestBody" in op:
            print("REQ", json.dumps(op["requestBody"]["content"]["application/json"]["schema"], indent=2)[:2500])

   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + Postgres/Mongo. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Active: lock remaining backend response shapes to OpenAPI spec
- Active: inspect leftover handlers + schema gaps
- Pending: build frontend matching UI contract
- Pending: app-setup scripts

COMPLETED:
- Surveyed OpenAPI contract schemas (WorkerJourneyPlan, RequesterJourneyPlan, Capacity, TimelineEntry, Location, LocationFunctionStates, OperationsLocation, OperationsConnection, ServiceabilityRegion, Role, LocationFunction, Certification, Coordinate)
- Read backend handlers: assignments.go, audit.go, serviceability.go, requests.go, util.go, idempotency.go, ws.go, network.go, journeys.go, work.go, users.go
- Read schema/postgres.sql, frontend scaffolding (api.ts, package.json, vite.config.ts, index.html, styles.css, tsconfig.json), README.md
- Read backend core: main.go, db.go, httpx.go, models.go, go.mod
- Identified contract mismatches in remaining handler responses
- Confirmed map assets at /opt/arena/map-assets (bangalore.pmtiles, fonts, sprites)

PENDING:
- Lock leftover backend handler response shapes to OpenAPI spec
- Finish remaining backend handlers
- Build React/Vite frontend matching UI contract
- App-setup scripts

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend is a Go 1.22 module `lablogistics` with Postgres (lib/pq) + Mongo audit + gorilla/websocket
- Frontend scaffold exists (Vite/React/TS, maplibre-gl + pmtiles) but UI not built out
- Schema at /workspace/schema/postgres.sql (journeys, assignments, locations, etc.)
- Contracts at /workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

message.content: I have a clear picture of the remaining contract mismatches. Next I’ll inspect the leftover handlers and then lock their response shapes to the OpenAPI spec.

function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

wanted = [
    "/api/collect-and-seal-sample",
    "/api/initiate-handoff",
    "/api/check-serviceability",
    "/api/list-role-work",
    "/api/read-sample-lifecycle",
    "/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}",
    "/api/read-journey-plan",
    "/api/create-connection",
    "/api/set-connection-status",
    "/api/configure-capacity",
    "/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance",
    "/api/create-sample-type",
    "/api/update-sample-type",
]
for p in wanted:
    methods = spec["paths"].get(p, {})
    for m, op in methods.items():
        print("="*70)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {p}  op={op.get('operationId')}  codes={list(op.get('responses',{}).keys())}")
        if "requestBody" in op:
            print("REQ", json.dumps(op["requestBody"]["content"]["application/json"]["schema"], indent=2)[:2000])

  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.

Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs; handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- inspect-contracts: IN_PROGRESS — comparing leftover handler shapes vs OpenAPI/UI contracts before locking responses
- lock-backend-shapes: PENDING — leftover handlers (handoff, role-work, lifecycle, journey-plan, serviceability, assignments)
- build-ui: PENDING — React/Vite frontend matching ui.contract.json scenarios
- app-setup: PENDING — setup scripts

COMPLETED:
- Inspected OpenAPI schemas: LocationFunctionStates, OperationsLocation, OperationsConnection, ServiceabilityRegion, LocationFunction
- Inspected backend files: assignments.go, serviceability.go, util.go, journeys.go, postgres.sql, mongo.js
- Inspected remaining handlers and frontend: work.go, users.go, network.go, db.go, idempotency.go, main.go, models.go, httpx.go, auth.go
- Inspected frontend: api.ts, styles.css, package.json (React 18 + Vite + maplibre-gl + pmtiles)
- Inspected ui.contract.json scenarios (login, role-switch, role-work, sample lifecycle/freshness)
- Workspace layout: INSTRUCTION.md, README.md, app-setup/, backend/, bin/, contracts/, frontend/, schema/

PENDING:
- Lock leftover backend response shapes to OpenAPI
- Build/complete UI for all ui.contract.json scenarios
- Write app-setup scripts
- End-to-end contract compliance

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend is substantial (auth, assignments, journeys, serviceability, network, work, users, idempotency, postgres+mongo)
- Contract mismatches identified; agent is locking leftover handler shapes then building UI + setup
- Key domain rules: dual-confirm handoffs, sender-responsible-until-complete, no duplicate custody, timeline on all custody changes, home samples need certified collector seal
- Frontend stack: React/Vite, maplibre-gl, pmtiles; roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab
- UI scenarios: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshness
- Sample types in api.ts: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse
- Leftover endpoints under review: /api/confirm-handoff, /api/record-worker-location, /api/list-role-work, /api/read-sample-lifecycle, /api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}, /api/read-journey-plan

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

Based on OpenHands security risk levels but adapted for agent-sdk.
Integer values allow for easy comparison and ordering.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `undo_edit`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory.

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

insert_line.description: Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`.

If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

3. When planning a complex refactoring, use this tool to outline different approaches and their tradeoffs.
4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open("/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json") as f:
    spec = json.load(f)
schemas = spec["components"]["schemas"]
for name in ["Location","Certification","Coordinate","LocationFunctions","OperationsLocation","OperationsConnection"]:
    print("="*70, name)
    print(json.dumps(schemas.get(name,{}), indent=2)[:2500])
    print()

# remaining paths
for path in [
    "/api/check-serviceability",
    "/api/read-serviceability-snapshot",
    "/api/read-sample-lifecycle",
    "/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}",
    "/api/list-role-work",
    "/api/read-journey-plan",
    "/api/read-operations-state",
    "/api/initiate-handoff",
    "/api/confirm-handoff",
    "/api/collect-and-seal-sample",
    "/api/record-worker-location",
    "/api/create-sample-type",
    "/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance",
    "/api/set-location-status",
    "/api/set-location-function-status",
    "/api/create-connection",
    "/api/set-connection-status",
    "/api/ui/bootstrap",
    "/ready",
]:
    methods = spec["paths"].get(path, {})
    print("="*70, path, list(methods))
    for m, op in methods.items():
        print("  opId", op.get("operationId"))
        print("  params", json.dumps(op.get("parameters", []), indent=2)[:600])
        if "requestBody" in op:
            sch = op["requestBody"]["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]
            print("  REQ", json.dumps(sch, indent=2)[:1800])
        for code in ["200","201"]:
            if code in op["responses"] and "content" in op["responses"][code]:
                sch = op["responses"][code]["content"]["application/json"]["schema"]
                print(f"  RESP {code}", json.dumps(sch, indent=2)[:2200])
PY","summary":"Dump remaining OpenAPI request/response shapes"}

* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:

2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.
